subject: BlueCrest - Hosted API degraded: CPU spike & delayed inference (status updates)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Kiran Patel <kiran@bluecrest.ai>, BlueCrest Ops <ops@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: BlueCrest - Hosted API degraded: CPU spike & delayed inference (initial alert)

Hi Kiran / BlueCrest team—

We detected a spike in CPU utilization affecting the hosted inference cluster that serves your production endpoint (model: gpt-redwood-small-v2). Starting 07:50 PDT we observed a sustained increase in 95th-percentile latency for generation requests to your account and a small number of 429s for short bursts. Our automated alerting opened an incident and we’ve started an ops bridge.

What we know so far:
- Impact: increased generation latency (p95 ~ 1.8s → 4.8s), intermittent 429s for high-concurrency customers on the affected pool.
- Scope: traffic from us-west cluster pool-7 where BlueCrest traffic is routed (you are currently in that pool).
- Detection: anomaly in kernel scheduling and a bad retry loop in an internal batching worker that created CPU contention.

Immediate mitigations in progress:
- We are prioritizing your routes and temporarily shifting a small percentage of traffic to a warm standby pool in us-east to reduce latency.
- Engineering is patching the worker to prevent the retry loop.

ETA: we expect a measurable improvement within 30–45 minutes, full resolution within 2 hours pending tests. I’ll post updates in this thread and publish to status.redwood.ai.

Attachments: incident_runbook.pdf (ops playbook), kernel_logs_excerpt.txt (current tail).

Sorry for the disruption — we’re working this actively and will keep you posted.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Ops & Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Kiran Patel <kiran@bluecrest.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:11:12 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueCrest - Hosted API degraded: CPU spike & delayed inference (initial alert)

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the quick note. Two quick asks: 1) Can you confirm whether inference requests processed during the window will be retried by Redwood or if we should dedupe on our side? 2) Any expected data loss or corrupted responses?

Also please confirm whether the failover to us-east will change the model latency profile for us (we optimize batching parameters on our side).

-Kiran
Kiran Patel
Head of ML Platform, BlueCrest Analytics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:25:46 -0700
Subject: Fwd: BlueCrest - Hosted API degraded: CPU spike & delayed inference (internal: action items)

Laura / Steph / Ben —

Looping you in for priority ops: BlueCrest is impacted by the CPU contention in pool-7. They’re the largest tenant on that pool this morning. Notes from monitoring: retry loop in sampler_worker causes threads to spin under certain edge-case payloads.

Immediate asks:
- Stephanie: coordinate controlled traffic shift for BlueCrest to us-east warm standby (start at 5% -> 25% if stable). Post routing change to status page and tell customer.
- Ben: prepare rollback and cost estimate for cross-region traffic for the hour window; we may need to credit tokens depending on impact.
- Laura: own external comms after the first recovery update; make sure messaging is clear and includes compensation options.

I’ve attached the runbook and the logs excerpt. Priority: high.

—Marcus
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: On-call Eng <oncall@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:47:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueCrest - Hosted API degraded: CPU spike & delayed inference (internal: action items)

On it. Summary of actions taken so far:
- Shifted ~10% of BlueCrest traffic to us-east warm pool at 08:35 PDT. Initial telemetry shows that p95 latency for that subset dropped to ~1.6s. No errors observed on failover subset.
- Patched sampler_worker to remove retry loop and deployed to the pool; patch currently in canary on two nodes.
- Keeping auto-scaling enabled, but cap reduced on pool-7 to prevent noisy neighbors while patch stabilizes.

Next steps:
- If canary is green (15m), increase traffic shift to 40% and continue monitoring.
- I'll coordinate with routing to do a more even distribution only if p95 for BlueCrest returns to baseline.

Will update customer now and publish to status.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Kiran Patel <kiran@bluecrest.ai>, BlueCrest Ops <ops@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:10:02 -0700
Subject: Update: CPU contention - partial mitigation in place (BlueCrest)

Hi Kiran — quick status update following our mitigation steps.

What we did:
- Temporarily routed ~10% of your live traffic to our us-east warm standby pool starting 08:35 PDT. That subset returned to expected latency (p95 ~1.6s).
- Deployed a targeted fix to an internal sampler_worker to stop the retry loop that was holding CPU. Canary looks good on two nodes.

Current impact:
- Customers still seeing degraded latency on the remaining traffic routed to the affected pool; we expect incremental improvement as we expand the shift.
- No evidence of corrupted responses or silent failures. If you issued a request that returned 429, that request was not retried by us automatically — we do not dedupe application-level retries. Please dedupe on your side if appropriate.

Next ETA: increase traffic shift to 40% after 15–20 minutes of stable telemetry; aiming for full resolution within 2 hours.

Compensation: we will issue a one-time credit for the incident window related to tokens billed during the degraded period. Ben will follow up with details.

Link to live status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270405-17

Thanks for your patience.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Ops & Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Kiran Patel <kiran@bluecrest.ai>, BlueCrest Ops <ops@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & draft postmortem: BlueCrest hosted inference degradation (INC-20270405-17)

Hi Kiran — following up with the investigation summary and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption; we know these incidents are costly for you.

Summary:
- Root cause: a rare retry loop in sampler_worker when handling a specific payload pattern under high concurrency. The loop caused unbounded CPU usage on nodes in pool-7, exacerbated by workload spikes, which pushed p95 latency up and caused transient 429s for queue rejections.
- Impact window: 2027-04-05T07:50:00Z → 2027-04-05T09:05:00Z (service normalized once traffic rerouting + patch completed).
- Customer-visible impact: increased p95 latency for generation requests and intermittent 429s for high-concurrency bursts. No response corruption or data loss.

Mitigations taken:
- Deployed patch removing the retry loop and restarted affected worker processes.
- Gradual traffic shift to a warm standby in us-east while the patch rolled out.
- Short-term routing policy change to prioritize affected routes for BlueCrest.

Longer-term actions (next 30 days):
- Replace sampler_worker retry logic with a bounded-backoff design and add unit + integration tests for the pattern that tripped the loop.
- Add a per-process CPU watchdog that can drain/replace noisy workers safely.
- Hardening: add a routing fallback that proactively migrates heavy tenants off a noisy pool if p95 exceeds threshold for 5 minutes.

Attachments: incident_postmortem_draft.pdf (internal draft); kernel_logs_excerpt.txt; incident_runbook.pdf

Compensation: Ben will issue a credit for billed tokens during the documented impact window; expect a billing note in 48 hours.

Next: we'll publish a short public postmortem to your account contact and the public status page after internal review. Please let us know if you’d like a short postmortem call — happy to schedule.

Thanks for your partnership,

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Ops & Reliability, Redwood Inference
